name: BLUEBIRD HOLDINGS LLC
address: 855 SW YATES STREET STE 101, BEND, OR 97702

fr.recommendations:
• Install reflective address numbers visible from the road at the driveway entrance.
• Mark which gate or access point provides the most direct route to the main residence.
• Keep all gates that provide emergency access unlocked or secured with a Knox-type lock box.
• Trim dense vegetation along walkways so responders can move between the main residence and detached structure without obstruction.
• Thin dense vegetation adjacent to the main residence and detached structure to create clear working space around both buildings.
• Clear a defined path between the vehicle parking area and the detached structure so responders can move equipment without navigating around obstacles.
• Mark the primary access point so arriving units do not lose time identifying the correct entry.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear enough for emergency vehicles to pull in without blocking their own exit.
• Identify and mark a turnaround point on the property so drivers of large emergency vehicles know where to reposition without backing blindly.
• Cut back dense vegetation that narrows the driveway or any path used to reach the detached structure.
• Post a simple site map near the main entry point showing the location of the main residence, detached structure, and any locked gates.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree clusters nearest to the structure to create open gaps between the trees and the building.
• Remove or trim shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure.
• Trim branches from scattered trees that hang over or lean toward the structure.
• Clear dead leaves, fallen branches, and dry plant material from the ground beneath tree clusters near the structure.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway to keep both access routes clear for vehicles.
• Remove shrubs and low branches growing along the driveway edges that could block or scratch passing vehicles.
• Separate the scattered shrubs from nearby tree clusters by removing shrubs growing beneath tree canopies.
• Keep the open terrain areas between tree clusters free of accumulated dead plant material.
• Thin vegetation along the driveway edges back far enough to allow a fire truck to pass without obstruction.
• Remove any shrubs or low branches within the open green space that have grown close enough to connect with tree clusters.
• Clear ground-level plant material from beneath tree clusters closest to the structure to reduce the chance of fire climbing from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Keep both access routes clear of fallen branches and overgrown vegetation year-round.
